nodes.label: Static page generation pipeline (ssg/)
nodes.rationale: ssg/routes.ts is the single source of truth and derives from the same data modules that render pages, so adding a product/industry/solution slug adds its prerendered route automatically.

nodes.label: App.tsx (lazy) / AppServer.tsx (eager) split
nodes.rationale: React.lazy is unsupported by renderToString, so the server variant keeps every page import static while the client variant code-splits. Both trees must stay structurally identical — including the Suspense boundary AppServer never actually suspends on.

nodes.label: __spa-fallback.html catch-all
nodes.rationale: Routes not in the manifest are served the original SPA shell so old URLs never break and new routes can be added incrementally; prerendered files match as exact statics before the catch-all is reached.

nodes.label: /console and /admin kept out of search (4 layers)
nodes.rationale: Layers don't stack for compliant crawlers — a bot obeying Disallow never reads the header — so the X-Robots-Tag layer exists purely for bots that ignore robots.txt and would otherwise get a plain 200 SPA shell carrying no robots meta.

nodes.label: src/lib/ssr-safe.ts compatibility layer
nodes.rationale: Only a couple of browser APIs needed guarding for SSR; everything else was already inside useEffect or event handlers. ZohoSignupForm defers its iframe until near-viewport, which also removed a geolocation prompt on page load.

nodes.label: Future migration to Vike
nodes.rationale: src/entry-server.tsx is the deliberate abstraction boundary; Vike becomes worth it only for incremental rendering, streaming SSR, partial hydration, edge rendering or on-demand SSR — none of which a fully data-driven static site needs today.
